title: Regime-Dependent Validity in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Evidence from SPARC Galaxy Rotation Curves and the EFC-R Framework
description: A pilot-scale analysis applying Energy-Flow Cosmology (EFC) to 20 SPARC galaxies spanning diverse morphological types, revealing regime-dependent validity where EFC achieves 100% success for LSB and diffuse dwarf galaxies but systematically underperforms for structurally complex systems. Introduces the EFC-R (Regime) framework with the decomposition E_total = E_flow + E_latent to delineate EFC's domain of validity.

energy_flow_field.description: Effective energy field governing circular velocities in EFC, where ρ is local energy density and S ∈ [0,1] is the normalized entropy field.

circular_velocity.description: EFC rotation velocity prediction derived from the energy-flow potential Φ_e.

delta_aic.description: Model comparison criterion: ΔAIC < −2 means EFC significantly preferred, ΔAIC > +2 means ΛCDM significantly preferred.

energy_decomposition.description: EFC-R regime decomposition separating the observable energy-flow component from latent energy contributions in structurally complex systems.

key_results.main_finding: EFC achieves 100% success rate for LSB and diffuse dwarf galaxies but 0% for barred/disturbed systems, with a statistically significant correlation between structural complexity and EFC performance (Spearman ρ = 0.705, p = 0.0005).

sealed_predictions.statement: EFC will maintain ≥90% success rate (ΔAIC ≤ 2) for LSB galaxies in an independent SPARC subsample of N ≥ 30 LSB systems.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: EFC success rate < 90% on a blind LSB sample of N ≥ 30 from SPARC.

sealed_predictions.statement: The Spearman correlation between the latent field proxy L and EFC residuals will remain significant (p < 0.01) when tested on the full SPARC sample (~175 galaxies).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Spearman p ≥ 0.01 on the full SPARC catalogue analysis.

sealed_predictions.statement: Barred and structurally disturbed galaxies will systematically require a non-zero E_latent contribution, showing ΔAIC > +2 for pure EFC fits.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Barred spirals fitting well under pure EFC (ΔAIC ≤ 2) without E_latent corrections.

kill_criteria: KC1: EFC success rate drops below 50% for LSB galaxies on an independent sample of N ≥ 50, invalidating the regime-dependent validity claim.
KC2: No statistically significant correlation (p < 0.05) between structural complexity proxy L and EFC fit quality is found on the full SPARC catalogue (N ~ 175).
KC3: The mean entropy gradient ∇S is not bounded within a physically plausible range across morphological types (e.g., ∇S varies by more than two orders of magnitude without systematic trend).
KC4: ΛCDM achieves uniformly lower χ²_red than EFC across all morphological categories including LSB and dwarf irregulars on an expanded sample.
KC5: An independent reanalysis of the same 20 galaxies using identical fitting procedures fails to reproduce the reported 80% success rate (i.e., obtains < 60%).

related_packages.role: Primary Figshare preprint deposit for the EFC-R SPARC pilot study.

name: EFC-R-SPARC
